title: Kotlin Multiplatform Warehouse App
subtitle: Rebuilding a 12-year-old system into a modular, shareable platform
overview: I rebuilt a legacy warehouse management app from the ground up using Kotlin Multiplatform. The old codebase was tangled after years of ad-hoc patches; the new approach focuses on a small, well-tested core and client-specific modules so teams can ship changes faster without stepping on each other's work.
challenge: The original app started on Windows Mobile, then shifted to Android with Java and XML over many years. It worked, but adding features or supporting a new client meant long, risky changes. Each customer had a slightly different fork and that made maintenance painful.
solution: I picked Kotlin Multiplatform to share logic across Android, iOS, desktop, and the web. I split the product into a core library and optional modules so a new client can reuse the core and only add the pieces they need. That reduced duplication and made releases predictable.

keyAchievements.title: Practical modular design
keyAchievements.description: Built a small core library for shared domain logic and separate modules for client-specific behavior. That made it possible to evolve the core independently from client customizations.

keyAchievements.title: ERP integrations
keyAchievements.description: Integrated with Oracle JDE and NetSuite so the same app can run in different environments without heavy rewrites.

keyAchievements.title: Fast path to production
keyAchievements.description: Delivered the first production rollout in about three months and scaled to multiple clients shortly after.

keyAchievements.title: Web distribution via WASM
keyAchievements.description: Added WebAssembly support so parts of the app can be served in a browser, reducing the need for frequent client updates.

keyAchievements.title: Hands-on technical leadership
keyAchievements.description: Acted as sole technical lead for the business unit, working directly with clients to shape priorities and avoid building features nobody needed.

learnings: A small, well-tested core prevents most duplication and makes shipping safer.
Talking to the actual users early avoids building shiny features no one needs.
Kotlin Multiplatform lets you share business logic without forcing one UI stack on everyone.
WASM can be surprisingly useful for distribution when you want to avoid frequent client updates.
